title: How Do Deep Networks Encode and Selectively Use Information? Shared Encoding and Conditional Signed Readout in Vision and Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.30854v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: How can trained deep networks retain contextual information across internal representations while using it selectively in a decision? We study this question through controlled background-texture edits in vision classifiers and entity-binding edits in frozen language models. Across both modalities, factor perturbations preserve recognizable structure across pre-fixed, mutually disjoint blocks of hidden units: visual channel blocks match their complements more closely for the same image than for other images under the same texture edit, while language blocks transfer a relational direction fitted under one query role to rank relational states within held-out name pairs under the other role. We then decompose the local output change into signed channel and pathway contributions. In a convolutional classifier, net channel-level reinforcement ($R^{(512)}>1$) coexists on individual images with cancellation between positive- and negative-weight

translated_title: 深度网络如何编码并选择性地使用信息？视觉与语言模型中的共享编码与条件性符号读出
translated_abstract: 训练好的深度网络如何在内部表示中保留上下文信息，同时在决策中选择性地使用这些信息？我们通过对视觉分类器进行受控的背景纹理编辑，以及对冻结语言模型进行实体绑定编辑来研究这一问题。在两种模态中，因子扰动在预先固定、互不相交的隐藏单元块之间保留了可识别的结构：在同一纹理编辑下，视觉通道块对同一图像与其补块的匹配程度高于对其他图像的匹配程度；而语言块能够将在一种查询角色下拟合的关系方向迁移到另一种角色下，用于对留出的姓名对中的关系状态进行排序。随后，我们将局部输出变化分解为带符号的通道贡献和通路贡献。在卷积分类器中，净通道级增强（R^(512)>1）在单个图像上与正负权重之间的抵消现象共存。
tldr: 该研究发现深度网络通过预先固定、互不相交的隐藏单元块共享编码上下文信息，并通过带符号的条件性读出机制在决策中选择性使用这些信息，这一机制在视觉分类器和冻结语言模型中均得到验证。
en_tdlr: The paper shows that deep networks encode contextual information in pre-fixed, mutually disjoint blocks of hidden units, and selectively use it for decisions via conditional signed readout, a mechanism validated in both vision classifiers and frozen language models.
